While Clairix is unlocked, an alert names what it found; locked, it says only \"Unlock to read\". Alerts never appear on the lock screen either way.
Every alert says only \"Unlock to read\"; what was found waits in the app. Alerts never appear on the lock screen either way.
Detection data stays on this phone. Export it when you want a record to keep or hand over.

The location log, the timeline, vehicle trips, the unlock ledger, the radio scanner\'s recordings and the map\'s tile and traffic caches older than this are deleted: now, at each start, every hour while scanning, and once a day otherwise. What is gone cannot be taken from the phone. Evidence you save about an app in Phone check, and photos you keep in the camera sweep, stay on the timeline until you clear all data. The cell-tower baseline is what normal is measured against, so it keeps which towers and areas are usual here and the last day each was seen (the exact time for two days), and forgets one not seen for three times this long (with Forever, never). An exported report is deleted after a day.
Erases everything Clairix holds on this phone and asks the relay to delete your account. The same page as Comms, menu, Wipe Clairix: type WIPE to confirm.

Detection data stays on this phone. Location history, device identifiers, cell tower baselines%1$s are stored locally, sealed under a key in this phone\'s secure hardware, and never uploaded. The map downloads tiles from %2$s\'s tile server, which sees your IP address and the area you\'re looking at; a place search runs on the phone over the offline map\'s road names and goes to OpenStreetMap\'s Nominatim service only when you choose to search online. Offline maps, work zones, the stalkerware list and the setting that names the tile server come signed from GitHub, and so, once a day, do the relay list, the keys those files are signed with and a note of the newest Clairix version. Messages and calls go through the Clairix relay, which cannot read them and is not told who sent them; live traffic is sent to it as anonymous road-segment speeds it can read but cannot tie to you. With Share traffic data on (Drive\'s route options) the box around a route you navigate or look at also goes through the relay to HERE and TomTom for incidents; they see the relay, not you. With push wake-ups set up, the relay sends your push server a POST saying only \"wake\" when something arrives; with Connect through Tor on, everything Clairix says to relays goes through the Tor network. Evidence leaves the phone only when you export it. Positions for the scanner, navigation and SOS come from %3$sAndroid\'s own location service; one worked out from Wi-Fi and cell towers sends their identifiers to that service, which on most phones is Google\'s, and so does the GPS check\'s comparison. Satellite-only positioning, under Location above, asks the satellites alone. With Also text this number on, under SOS above, an SOS also goes as an ordinary, unencrypted text through your mobile carrier to that number.

Messages and calls are end-to-end encrypted; the relay sees neither what they say nor who sent them. Your keys, contacts and history are stored on this phone only. Location is read at the moment you press SOS, to attach to that alert, and at no other time. That position comes from %1$sAndroid\'s own location service; one worked out from Wi-Fi and cell towers sends their identifiers to that service. Satellite-only positioning, under Location above, asks the satellites alone. Once a day Clairix fetches the signed relay list, the keys it is signed with and a note of the newest version from GitHub; nothing about you goes with the request. With push wake-ups set up, the relay sends your push server a POST saying only \"wake\" when something arrives, so it learns when, not what or from whom; with Connect through Tor on, everything Clairix says to relays goes through the Tor network. With Also text this number on, under SOS above, an SOS also goes as an ordinary, unencrypted text through your mobile carrier to that number.
